title: Practice
subtitle: DSE-style Maths, M1, M2 and Physics questions with marking schemes, instant MC feedback and AI marking of your written work.
subject: Subject

generate.title: Get a question
generate.description: We serve a checked question from the shared bank that you haven't seen. If none fits, we write a new one.
generate.bankFirst: Free when served from the bank.
generate.typeHint: Any topic: choose the question type and difficulty.
generate.descriptionLocal: We write a new DSE-style question for you, checked by code. It's saved in this browser.
generate.localNote: Questions are saved on this device.

reference.intro: Photograph a worksheet or textbook question (or type it). We'll tell you what we understood, then write new questions like it.
reference.orType: Or type the question (describe any figure in words)
reference.typePlaceholder: e.g. In the figure, ∠B = 90°, AB = 5 cm and BC = 12 cm. Find AC.
reference.understoodHint: Check and fix anything before generating. Maths is written in LaTeX between $ signs.
reference.figureUnsupported: This figure can't be drawn yet: {note}
reference.figureProblems: The figure may not match the numbers: {problems}
reference.figureJsonHint: The figure is drawn from this JSON. Leave it empty for no figure.
reference.variation: How different should the new questions be?

1.name: 1 · Number swap
1.description: Same wording and figure, new numbers.

2.name: 2 · New context
2.description: Same maths and method in a new setting.

3.name: 3 · New structure
3.description: Same idea, but a different unknown or an extra step.

reference.privateNote: Questions from your reference are private to you.
reference.made: {count, plural, one {# question ready} other {# questions ready}}
reference.privateNoteLocal: Questions from your reference are saved on this device.

typePlaceholders.math_m1: e.g. Let f(x) = x e^(1/(x−2)). (a) Find f′(x). (b) Someone claims the curve y = f(x) has only one horizontal tangent. Do you agree? Explain.
typePlaceholders.math_m2: e.g. Let f(x) = 1/(3x² + 4). Find f′(x) from first principles.

question.solutionAfter: The solution and community answers unlock after you answer.
question.solutionAfterLocal: The solution unlocks after you answer.
question.showAnswer: Show answer (no need to answer first)

solution.analysis: 解題 — how to approach it
solution.codeChecksNote: Each result is tested at random points (derivatives against finite differences, integrals against numerical integration). Proofs, explanations and verdicts are not code-verified.

answer.title: Your answer
answer.description: Write your working on paper, then photograph it. We transcribe it to LaTeX exactly as written; you check it before marking.
answer.upload: {count, plural, =0 {Upload and transcribe} one {Upload # page and transcribe} other {Upload # pages and transcribe}}
answer.markHint: Marked like the DSE: method (M) and answer (A) marks.

transcript.hint: Check each line against your paper. Fix only reading mistakes — not your maths, or the marking won't reflect your work.

result.stillMarking: Your answer is still being marked…
result.notMarked: This attempt hasn't been marked yet.
result.solutionLocked: The solution unlocks once your answer is marked.

dispute.title: Dispute: {label}
dispute.description: Tell us why you think this is marked wrongly. Disputes are reviewed to improve the marker; your score doesn't change now.
dispute.placeholder: e.g. My line 4 uses the cosine rule correctly, so the M mark should be awarded.
dispute.descriptionLocal: Note why you think this is marked wrongly. In local mode disputes are saved on this device only; your score doesn't change.

recent.title: Recent attempts
recent.empty: No attempts yet. Get a question to start.

solve.intro: Type or photograph any physics question. The AI finds the syllabus topic and writes the answer and a DSE-style marking scheme, with 解題 thinking and tips.
solve.photo: Add photos of the question (several pages are fine)
solve.text: Or type the question (and anything else it needs, like the options)
solve.placeholder: e.g. A car of mass 1200 kg accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m s⁻¹ in 8 s. (a) Find the acceleration…
solve.note: Saved on this device under My questions. Answers are checked by code where possible.
solve.pagesNote: {count} photos will be read as one question, in this order — use the arrows to reorder pages.
